children.text: śatāvaryādirasamarditakāśīśādibhiḥ saha puṭitasya yavaciñcārasena piṣṭirvā kāryeti piṣṭidvayam
children.translated_text: Or, from material heated in a puṭa together with kāśīśa and the other substances after trituration with the juice of śatāvarī and the rest, a piṣṭi should be made with the juice of yavaciñcā: thus there are two piṣṭis.
And likewise in that same work:
Taking, goddess, dhānyābhraka mixed with the sour group,
one should decoct that mica and triturate it with the milk of snuhī.
Then, with wild cow-dung, one should give it the puṭa called kapota.
With the exudations of plantain tubers and with the juice of radish tubers,
with kākamācī, mīnākṣī, apāmārga, and muni,
with eraṇḍa, fresh ginger, meghanāda, and punarnavā,
one should give one puṭa with the liquids of each one successively.
Joined with the milk of vajrī, it should be cooked in a swing-apparatus.
After drying it in the shade, with chickpea sour liquid, O <s>Bhairavī</s>,

children.text: ghanasāraṃ ca kāśīśaṃ vacā nimbaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: ghanasāra, kāśīśa, vacā, and nimba as well,
each one-sixteenth part of the mica should be placed there.

children.text: nidhāya tāmrapātre tu gharṣayettaṃ ca suvrate ||
children.translated_text: Having put it in a copper vessel, he should rub it, O virtuous one.

children.text: navavāraṃ tato devi lohapātre tu jārayet
children.translated_text: Then, nine times, goddess, he should digest it in an iron vessel.
Together with <s>rasa</s>, O mistress of gods, chickpea sour liquid is the kāñjika.
It should be boiled down over a gentle fire; it is produced in half a prahara.
Having ground vyoman with the juices of somavallī and mixed it with sauvarcala salt,
one should slowly give three puṭas with haṃsapāka heating.
With somavallī juice alone one should treat it seven times.
With somavallī juice alone one should apply it seven times.
One should cast it down into an earthen vessel, soaked together with <s>rasa</s>.
The root of vallīṣupuṅkhā should be rubbed with cow's milk.
With the paste one should smear mercury and the gagana placed above it.
He should heat it by the sun's heat; without opening its mouth it swallows at once.

children.text: jāyate piṣṭikā śīghraṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
children.translated_text: A piṣṭikā is produced quickly; no doubt should be entertained here.
Thus, by heating in a puṭa, there is another, third piṣṭi.
With the juice of tilaparṇī alone, one should treat gagana with it.
From trituration a piṣṭi is produced; no doubt should be entertained here.
The remainder is: 'heated in a puṭa by the previously stated method.'
Thus there is another piṣṭi.
Thus there are four piṣṭis of mica, arka, powder, and piṣṭi.
Now the piṣṭi of the essence of vyoman, in the <s>Rasārṇava</s>:
The essence of vyoman, melted and purified with glass and borax,
by applications of sour tamarind fruit and paste of sehuṇḍa leaves,
should be cooked and prepared, goddess; it becomes equal to mercury-piṣṭi.
In the <s>Rasaratnākara</s> too:
Having melted the essence of mica, one should add an equal part of glass and borax.
Having given that again and again three times, he should blow it in a diamond crucible.
The sour group, snuhī leaves, and tamarind seeds with their bark
should be made into a paste; in that he should quench that essence seven times.

children.text: mṛdu śubhraṃ bhavettacca hitaṃ sūtasya jāraṇe ||
children.translated_text: It becomes soft and white, and is useful for the digestion of mercury.
Now the sulphur piṣṭi.
In the <s>Rasaratnapradīpikā</s>:

children.text: viloḍite svarṇajale viśuṣke vastre'tha dattvā navanītagarbham
children.translated_text: When svarṇajala has been stirred and dried, then, after placing a core of fresh butter in a cloth,
there is the powder of śilātālaka, sulphur, and pannaga, in equal portions.

children.text: karṣapramāṇāṃ tu tato'sya vartiṃ prajvālayettadgalitaṃ ghṛtaṃ syāt
children.translated_text: Then he should light a wick of one karṣa in measure; its melted substance should become ghee.
With this he should everywhere make a paste of the lord of <s>rasa</s>, for the digestion by bali.
Also in the <s>Rasendracintāmaṇi</s>:
One pala of purified mercury and one karṣa of sulfur
should be placed in a heated mortar, soaked with the juice of <s>devadālī</s>.
He should triturate it with the fingers of the hand; a sulfur paste is produced.

children.text: bhāgā dvādaśa sūtasya dvau bhāgau gandhakasya ca ||
children.translated_text: Twelve parts of mercury and two parts of sulfur
should be triturated with the addition of ghee; a sulfur paste is produced.
And elsewhere:
One pala of powdered sulfur, with liquids produced from the fruits of <s>bṛhatī</s>,
with the fresh juices of <s>ākāśavallī</s>, and with cow urine, should be impregnated.
Each should be dried after twenty-one repetitions.
It should also be impregnated with the sour group and with the red and yellow group.
When dried, the essence should be carefully obtained by means of the <s>śrīraṅga</s> apparatus.
With the liquid from that apparatus itself, a paste is made for digesting mercury.
Or sulfur and the other pastes, impregnated by the previously stated extraction of color, are used.
Thus the sulfur paste.
Now the paste of <s>śilātāla</s>, in the <s>Rasārṇava</s>:
With the groups of oily, alkaline, and sour substances, three puṭas are to be given to <s>śilā</s>.
In a cauldron, in a fumigation apparatus, through an application of fumigating aromatics,

children.text: vaṃgasya hi vidhānena tālasya hatasya ca
children.translated_text: according to the procedure for tin and for killed <s>tāla</s>,

children.text: tāpyahiṃgulayor vāpi hīnaṃ vai rasakasya vā ||
children.translated_text: or also for <s>tāpya</s> and cinnabar, or indeed deficient <s>rasaka</s>.
<s>Devendragiri</s> says:
An essence measuring one sixteenth of the mercury should be smeared on a crucible, sealed, and heated in a puṭa.
It is put in a fire with husk-fuel of one karṣa until only the mercury remains.
In this same way another essence-paste should be made from the essences stated in the class of metals.
Thus the paste of <s>śilātāla</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, and the like.
Now, in the <s>Rasārṇava</s>, the gold and silver bījas:
Now then I shall explain the preparation of the bījas, beloved.
According to gold and silver, the bīja is twofold, O queen.
A golden bīja is made with yellow and red substances; a silver bīja is made with white ones.

children.text: kalpitaṃ rañjitaṃ pakvam iti bhūyastridhā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: It is further threefold: prepared, colored, and cooked.
There the prepared kind is twofold, by the distinction of pure and mixed.
The prepared bījas of <s>rasa</s>, secondary minerals, and metals are separate.
The pure is separate; the mixed, O queen of gods, is made by combination according to availability.
Mixed kinds include gold-mica, copper-mica, silver-mica, tin-mica, lead-mica, lodestone-mica, and so on.
Thus the prepared bījas.

children.text: atha tatraiva rañjitabījāni bījāni kalpitānyevaṃ rañjitāni paraṃ śṛṇu
children.translated_text: Now, in that same work, the colored bījas: Listen further to the bījas prepared in this way and then colored.
Dense mica is colored with pyrite powder and copper powder.
When combined with the essence of <s>tāpya</s>, it colors the king of <s>rasa</s>.
With red creepers and urines, repeatedly impregnated in many ways,
with <s>kunaṭī</s>, sulfur, stones, gold pyrites, and cinnabar,
vaporized, sprinkled with the red groups, killed with oils, and then
colored, especially sharp copper colors the king of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: kevalaṃ vimalaṃ tāmraṃ vāpitaṃ daradena vā
children.translated_text: Pure refined copper alone, or vaporized with cinnabar,
when digested threefold, makes the mercury resemble lac juice.
Having added twice as much <s>rasaka</s>, well-smelted copper, O queen,

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrakasya cūrṇaṃ ca raktavarṇaṃ muhuḥ puṭaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and powder of black mica, red in color through repeated puṭas,

children.text: tāpyena vā mṛtaṃ hema triguṇena vipācitam
children.translated_text: or gold killed with <s>tāpya</s> and cooked with three times as much,
and <s>rasaka</s> in a pot, combined with <s>tāpya</s> and rock salt,
until it resembles an <s>indragopa</s> insect, by twofold digestion of all,
makes mercury resemble molten gold; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: abhrakaṃ hema tāmraṃ ca śilayā mākṣikeṇa ca
children.translated_text: Mica, gold, and copper should be colored with <s>śilā</s> and <s>mākṣika</s>,

children.text: gairikeṇa ca mukhyena rasakena ca rañjayet ||
children.translated_text: and with the principal red ochre and with <s>rasaka</s>.
Or gold extracted by <s>kunaṭī</s>-killed iron, by copper killed with <s>tāpya</s> and sulfur,
or by iron struck with cinnabar: that is the bīja.
But in the <s>Rasasāra</s>, the operation of mixing:
At the very beginning one should make the proper mixture of the bījas.
Having brought all the bījas through, he should vaporize them by sprinkling.

children.text: tāpyaṃ vā rasakaṃ vāpi haṃsaṃ vā vimalāṃ śilām
children.translated_text: <s>Tāpya</s>, or <s>rasaka</s>, or <s>haṃsa</s>, or pure <s>śilā</s>
should constantly be vaporized into all the bījas by one skilled in sprinkling.
Sprinkling with red liquid is especially the coloring.
All the bījas become colored; there is no doubt.
The mercury and the secondary minerals, all red and yellow,
are threefold, extracted with gold; the remaining gold is the bīja.

children.text: tad bījaṃ cārayetsūte samabhāgaṃ ca kārayet
children.translated_text: One should make that bīja enter into mercury and make the two equal in quantity.
Having colored the mercury, he should make it flow with an equal bīja.
Here the entry and flowing of the prepared and cooked bījas are exactly the same.
In the <s>Rasendracintāmaṇi</s>:

children.text: karṣāṣṭaṃkaṇakajjalīharihayairgandhasya ca dvau rajaḥ siddhākhyaṃ sakalaiḥ kṛtaṃ palamatha dvitraiśca lohaiḥ śṛtam
children.translated_text: Eight karṣas of gold, collyrium, and green vitriol, and two of sulfur powder, called siddha, made with all substances, then one pala cooked with two or three metals,

children.text: bhūyo gandhamṛtaṃ caturdaśapuṭaiḥ syādindragopāruṇaṃ tattāre madhunā puṭena dhamanenārkacchavīmīhate ||
children.translated_text: again becomes killed sulfur by fourteen puṭas, red like an <s>indragopa</s>; when applied to that silver with honey, by puṭa and blowing it seeks the color of the sun.

children.text: tulyaṃ tāre tāmramāvartya tāvattaptaṃ taptaṃ gandhacūrṇe kunaṭyām
children.translated_text: Having melted copper equal to the silver, as long as it is hot, hot, in powdered sulfur and <s>kunaṭī</s>,
it is placed there until it is digested piece by piece; then one should cook it in a glass bottle with abundant sulfur.
That same substance, having the form of pieces, with borax, placed inside gold and within an ash-crucible,

children.text: dhmātaṃ sādhu syāt suvarṇaṃ satāraṃ hīne varṇe rañjayenmākṣikeṇa ||
children.translated_text: when well blown, becomes good gold with silver; if the color is deficient, one should color it with <s>mākṣika</s>.
Now, in the <s>Rasārṇava</s>, the cooked bījas:
Having thus colored the bījas, now listen to the cooked bīja.
One should add the great rasas, the secondary rasas, and the sharp metals.
With an equal portion of <s>mākṣika</s> and by the application of sulfur as an admixture,
one should cause this to be carried through a hundred times, not deficient and with a residue left.
With an equal portion of the king of <s>rasa</s>, it certainly melts in the womb.
This is praised, O queen of gods, in fixing the paste and in digestion,
in coloring the king of <s>rasa</s>, and also in making it flow.
That same substance, sprinkled a hundred times with the oils of the red group,
is praised as superior among them, making penetration by a thousandth part.
Drawn out with lead and tin, it is used in the operation on gold and silver.
The essence of <s>kha</s> should be joined with the sun-metal; when paired, it is effective in alchemy.
With oily, alkaline, pungent, and sour juices, and with those such as <s>tālaka</s>,
one should carry tin and lead into copper in equal, double, or triple measure.
That, sprinkled with red oil, is remembered as the extraction of <s>rasa</s>.
<s>Mākṣika</s>, sulfur-stone, orpiment, realgar,
<s>vaikrāntaka</s>, lodestone and the like, <s>sasyaka</s>, and pure collyrium,
and also <s>rasaka</s>, powdered a hundred times, should be carried into gold.
By iron foil, <s>tāpya</s>, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, pure mica,
killed copper, stone, mercury, the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, and cinnabar,

children.text: nāgo nirjīvatāṃ yāti puṭayogaiḥ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: lead becomes lifeless through repeated applications of puṭa heating.
So too tin, with <s>rasa</s>, orpiment, conch, tamarind, and alkalis.

children.text: mṛtaṃ nāgaṃ mṛtaṃ vaṃgaṃ śulbaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ tathā mṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Killed lead, killed tin, copper, and sharp iron, likewise killed,
each one should be carried into the finest gold, O worshipped by the gods.

children.text: nirutthe pannage hemni nirvyūḍhe śataśo guṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When lead has become non-rising in gold and has been drawn out a hundred times by qualities,
the gold becomes like <s>gorocanā</s>, solar, and resembling silver.
Sharp iron and mica equal to the sun-metal, and twice as much <s>mākṣika</s>,

children.text: āvartitaṃ cūrṇitaṃ ca māritaṃ saptabhiḥ puṭaiḥ
children.translated_text: having been melted, powdered, and killed with seven puṭas,
when carried a hundredfold into gold, should be digested as an equal bīja.
It should penetrate silver and gold by a hundredth part through coating the leaves.

children.text: ūrdhvādho mākṣikaṃ dattvā śulbaṃ hemasamaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When <s>mākṣika</s> is placed above and below, copper becomes equal to gold.
Thus the bīja, carried tenfold and resembling rays,
should then be blown with <s>rasaka</s>, mica, and copper, increasing by portions.
And that, struck with <s>mākṣika</s>, should be carried through into the bīja, beloved.
Lead, struck with <s>tāpya</s>, should be carried thirty-twofold into gold.
A lead-bīja is said to have a thirtyfold admixture of realgar.
But by an admixture of <s>tāpya</s> and orpiment, the essence of yellow mica
should carry this bīja through; it penetrates what has been extracted from bell-metal.

children.text: nāgaḥ karoti mṛdutāṃ nirvyūḍhastāṃ ca raktatām ||
children.translated_text: Lead, when drawn out, produces softness and also redness.

children.text: vāpitaṃ pītatāṃ tīkṣṇaṃ kāntasthāṃ kālikāṃ viṣam
children.translated_text: When admixed, sharp iron makes yellowness; lodestone takes on blackness, and poison likewise.
Something similar is stated in the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:

children.text: svarṇaṃ tāmraṃ samaṃ śuddhaṃ drāvitaṃ lepayetpunaḥ
children.translated_text: Pure gold and copper in equal amounts, melted together, should again be coated.
With an acidic combination of <s>tāpya</s>, one should blow it until only the gold remains.

children.text: evaṃ daśaguṇaṃ vāhyaṃ tāmraṃ vā tutthasattvakam
children.translated_text: In this way copper, or the essence of blue vitriol, should be carried tenfold.
Known as the cooked bīja, the remaining gold should be collected.
And similarly, more fully, in the <s>Rasasāra</s>:
Red mica, gold, <s>rasaka</s>; gold-mica, quicksilver, realgar;
<s>mākṣika</s>, lodestone, and sharp iron; gold, <s>mākṣika</s>, and mica;
gold, lodestone, and <s>mākṣika</s>; sharp iron and <s>mākṣika</s> with gold;
red sharp iron and <s>mākṣika</s>; lodestone-mica; <s>tāpya</s> and gold;
black mica, gold, and sharp iron; copper, lodestone, and sharp iron;

children.text: mākṣikaṃ gaganaṃ hemaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ tāmraṃ ca mākṣikam ||
children.translated_text: <s>mākṣika</s>, mica, gold, sharp iron, copper, and <s>mākṣika</s>;
yellow mica, lodestone, and sharp iron; lodestone, copper, and <s>mākṣika</s>;
sharp iron, mica, copper, and <s>mākṣika</s>; copper, sharp iron, mica, and gold;
copper, lodestone, and sharp iron; sharp iron, lodestone, and copper;

children.text: mākṣikaṃ gaganaṃ hema tīkṣṇatāmraṃ ca mākṣikam ||
children.translated_text: <s>mākṣika</s>, mica, gold, sharp iron, copper, and <s>mākṣika</s>;
copper, lodestone, mica, and <s>mākṣika</s>; sharp sun-metal, lead, and <s>mākṣika</s>;
gold, mica, sun-metal, and sharp iron; gold, mica, copper, and <s>mākṣika</s>;
gold, mica, mercury, and copper; mercury, tin, mica, and gold;

children.text: rūkma vyoma khagaṃ kāntaṃ sasyābhraṃ kāñcanaṃ khagam ||
children.translated_text: gold, mica, mercury, and lodestone; <s>sasya</s>, mica, gold, and mercury;

children.text: rūkma vyoma khagaṃ haṃsaṃ tutthābhraṃ khagakāñcanam
children.translated_text: gold, mica, mercury, and <s>haṃsa</s>; blue vitriol, mica, mercury, and gold;

children.text: rūkma vyoma khagaṃ śailaṃ rūkma vyoma khagaṃ trapu ||
children.translated_text: gold, mica, mercury, and stone; gold, mica, mercury, and tin;

children.text: rūkma vyoma raviścauraṃ tālābhraṃ kāñcanaṃ khagam
children.translated_text: gold, mica, sun-metal, and copper; orpiment, mica, gold, and mercury;

children.text: rūkma vyoma khagaṃ ghoṣaṃ rūkma vyoma khagāñjanam ||
children.translated_text: gold, mica, mercury, and bell-metal; gold, mica, mercury, and collyrium;

children.text: rūkma vyoma khagaṃ brāhmaṃ rūkma vyoma khagaṃ śilā
children.translated_text: gold, mica, mercury, and <s>brāhma</s>; gold, mica, mercury, and realgar;
gold, mercury, tin, and copper; mercury, iron, copper, and gold;

children.text: rūkma coraṃ khagaṃ śailaṃ rūkma coraṃ ca mākṣikam
children.translated_text: gold, copper, mercury, and stone; gold, copper, and <s>mākṣika</s>;
gold, copper, mercury, and <s>sasya</s>; copper, <s>vaikrānta</s>, and <s>mākṣika</s>;

children.text: rūkma coraṃ khagaṃ gandhaṃ rūkma coraṃ khagaṃ malam
children.translated_text: gold, copper, mercury, and sulfur; gold, copper, mercury, and impurity;

children.text: rūkma śilā khagaṃ coraṃ rūkma coraṃ khagāñjanam ||
children.translated_text: gold, realgar, mercury, and copper; gold, copper, mercury, and collyrium;

children.text: rūkma coraṃ khagaṃ tutthaṃ kāsīsaṃ coramākṣikam
children.translated_text: gold, copper, mercury, and blue vitriol; green vitriol, copper, and <s>mākṣika</s>;

children.text: rūkma coraṃ khagaṃ kāṃkṣī rūkma coraṃ khagaṃ trapu ||
children.translated_text: gold, copper, mercury, and alum; gold, copper, mercury, and tin;

children.text: rūkma coraṃ khagaṃ nāgaṃ coraṃ rādhoṣamākṣikam ||
children.translated_text: gold, copper, mercury, and lead; copper, bell-metal, and <s>mākṣika</s>;

children.text: rūkma coraṃ khagaṃ śulbaṃ rāścauraṃ khagamākṣikam
children.translated_text: gold, copper, mercury, and copper; <s>rā</s>, copper, mercury, and <s>mākṣika</s>;

children.text: rūkma coraṃ khagaṃ śulvaṃ rāścauraṃ khagamākṣikam
children.translated_text: gold, copper, mercury, and copper; <s>rā</s>, copper, mercury, and <s>mākṣika</s>;

children.text: rūkma coraṃ śilāṃ haṃsaṃ coraṃ rā haṃsamākṣikam ||
children.translated_text: gold, copper, realgar, and <s>haṃsa</s>; copper, <s>rā</s>, <s>haṃsa</s>, and <s>mākṣika</s>.
<s>Nāga</s>, <s>rārasaka</s>, <s>haṃsa</s>, <s>haṃsa</s>, <s>rācora-mākṣika</s>;
<s>rāśulva</s>, <s>rasaka</s>, <s>haṃsa</s>, <s>rāścora</s>, and mountain cinnabar.
<s>Cora</s>, <s>rādarada</s>, <s>cora</s>, <s>haṃsa</s>, <s>rācora-hiṃgula</s>;
iron, <s>rādarada</s>, <s>cora</s>, cinnabar, and sharp <s>coraka</s>.

children.text: kāṃkṣī ca hiṃgulaṃ coraṃ rākāṃkṣī corahiṃgulam
children.translated_text: Alum and cinnabar, <s>cora</s>; <s>rākāṃkṣī</s> and <s>cora-hiṃgula</s>;

children.text: haṃsaṃ rārasakaṃ coraṃ punarbījaṃ ca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>haṃsa</s>, <s>rārasaka</s>, and <s>cora</s>: again a bīja is produced.

children.text: hemaikaṃ triguṇaṃ coraṃ hemaikaṃ triguṇaṃ khagam
children.translated_text: One part gold with three parts <s>cora</s>; one part gold with three parts <s>khaga</s>;

children.text: hemaikaṃ triguṇaṃ haṃsaṃ hemaikaṃ triguṇaṃ giriḥ ||
children.translated_text: one part gold with three parts <s>haṃsa</s>; one part gold with three parts <s>giri</s>.
One part gold with three parts <s>tāla</s>; one part gold with three parts <s>vimalā</s>;
or gold one part with thrice-calcined lead; one part gold with three parts <s>śilā</s>.

children.text: hemaikaṃ triguṇaṃ tutthaṃ hemaikaṃ triguṇaṃ vaṭam
children.translated_text: One part gold with three parts <s>tuttha</s>; one part gold with three parts <s>vaṭa</s>;

children.text: hemaikaṃ triguṇā rīrī hemaikaṃ ca tritutthakam ||
children.translated_text: one part gold with three parts <s>rīrī</s>; and one part gold with triple <s>tuttha</s>.

children.text: hemaikaṃ triguṇaṃ ghoṣaṃ hemaikaṃ triguṇaṃ trapu
children.translated_text: One part gold with three parts <s>ghoṣa</s>; one part gold with three parts tin;
one part gold with three parts lead: bīja has been taught in many ways.
Here each single quarter-verse has been arranged as a bīja individually;
and again, through the procedure of repeated application, the bījas are endless.
From the essences of ores and stones produced in various deposits,
and from combinations of <s>rasa</s> and secondary minerals, one should prepare the excellent bīja.
With all the bījas together or separately, and also made in increasing proportions,
when they have been digested in gold in triple quantity, transmutation successively reaches up to a hundredfold.
The number consisting of <s>rasa</s>, graha, and ravi-stambha increases by thirtyfold;

children.text: uttamaṃ kanakaṃ jāryaṃ kramavṛddhyā ca vedhakṛt ||
children.translated_text: excellent gold is to be digested, and by gradual increase it produces transmutation.
And in mercury, by increase of parts, it is twenty- and thirtyfold greater;

children.text: viṣamaṃ vā samaṃ vātha samaṃ viṣamameva ca ||
children.translated_text: whether uneven or even, or even and then uneven.
When the bīja has been digested according to the sequence of the number of colors, it brings about transmutation.
Here <s>khaga</s> means green vitriol,
<s>cora</s> means calamine,
<s>haṃsa</s> means cinnabar,
<s>brāhma</s> means copper,
and <s>rā</s> means gold.
The numbering beginning with <s>rasa</s> will become clear in mercuries that effect thousandfold and higher transmutation.

children.text: sahasravedhake ṣaḍguṇitair ayutavedhake navaguṇitair lakṣavedhake dvādaśaguṇitaiḥ prayutavedhake pañcadaśaguṇitaiḥ koṭivedhake'ṣṭādaśaguṇitai raktābhrādibhir jīrṇaiḥ kanakaṃ bījaṃ syādityarthaḥ
children.translated_text: That is, for a thousandfold transmuting mercury gold is the bīja when digested with red mica and the like multiplied sixfold; for a ten-thousandfold one, ninefold; for a hundred-thousandfold one, twelvefold; for a millionfold one, fifteenfold; and for a crore-fold one, eighteenfold.
And again in that same work:
Of iron, <s>ghoṣa</s>, silver, and copper, the portions are one, two, and three grahas respectively;
lead is in the portion called <s>stithi</s>; all of it should be smelted until half remains.

children.text: rañjanīyaṃ same jīrṇe kanake syāt subījakam
children.translated_text: When what is to be colored has been digested in equal gold, it becomes a good bīja.
When the bīja has been digested and made to flow, the mercury becomes capable of hundredfold transmutation.
Of gold, lead, and copper, each is to be a graha portion;
of brass, sharp iron, and <s>ghoṣa</s>, the portions are multiplied by veda and pakṣa;
the remainder in gold becomes the bīja that causes hundredfold transmutation.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ tāmraṃ samaṃ kṛtvā nāgaṃ nirvāhya ṣaḍguṇam
children.translated_text: Having made sharp iron and copper equal, one should carry lead through in sixfold quantity;
what remains as copper becomes red, drawn out with gold, and is a good bīja.

children.text: nāge ca triguṇā rītirnāgaṃ tāmraṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: In lead there is threefold brass, and lead and copper likewise;
that copper, drawn out with gold, becomes an excellent bīja.
Gold is made eight parts, red copper four parts,
and lead two parts; the whole, with gold remaining, is the bīja.
The eight metals, all the rasas, and likewise the secondary minerals,

children.text: ekatra melanaṃ kṛtvā lohaśeṣaṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: should be combined in one place, and one should make the metal remain.
That, digested in mercury in thirty-twofold quantity, is this great bīja;
one should likewise digest a gold bīja in twenty-twofold quantity.
In the <s>Rasaratnākara</s>:
One should kill copper with <s>tāpya</s>, and likewise when it has been killed with sulfur,

children.text: tat tāmraṃ vāhayennāge mūṣāmadhye dhaman dhaman ||
children.translated_text: one should carry that copper into lead inside a crucible, blowing again and again.
Slowly, until it is a hundredfold, one should keep adding powdered <s>tāpya</s>;
then one should carry that lead into gold, gradually, in thirty-twofold quantity.
The remaining gold is that bīja; one should digest it in mercury in equal portion.
With this very bīja one should again digest and make it flow.
By the digestion procedures as before, one should bring it to the point of fixation,
and, joined with penetration, it should transmute with a thousandth part.
The moon-and-sun metal becomes gold, excellent as an ornament for the gods.

children.text: svarṇaṃ tāmraṃ samaṃ śuddhaṃ drāvitaṃ lepayetpunaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Pure gold and copper, equal and melted, should then be smeared;
with an acidic <s>tāpya</s> preparation one should blow it until gold remains.

children.text: evaṃ daśaguṇaṃ vāhyaṃ tāmraṃ vā tutthasattvakam
children.translated_text: Thus copper should be carried through tenfold, or else the essence of <s>tuttha</s>.
What remains as gold should be collected; it is known as a cooked bīja.
Now the cooked silver bījas, in the <s>Rasārṇava</s>:
The gold bīja has been explained; now listen to the silver bīja.
Sharp iron, mica, <s>tāpya</s>, <s>vimalā</s>, and <s>rasaka</s> are in equal parts;
there are four parts of tin; the whole, smelted and pulverized,

children.text: puṭena nihataṃ kāryaṃ vyūḍhaṃ tāraṃ tu vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: should be killed by a puṭa. When drawn out, it should transmute silver.

children.text: dvātriṃśacca guṇaṃ tāre vaṃgaṃ tāpyahataṃ vahet
children.translated_text: Tin killed by <s>tāpya</s> should be carried into silver in thirty-twofold quantity,
and thirtyfold <s>tālaka</s>; this is called the tin bīja.
